mapping_basis: Pictures follow the intake naming convention: NNN.jpg is the first picture whose own Facebook caption states stanza #N; NNN-2.jpg and later are further pictures for that stanza; nostanza-NN.jpg have no stated stanza and stay unmapped. A picture whose caption labels several stanzas (for example "#5 & #6") is mapped to each of them. Source photos are contextual references only; canonical Sanskrit governs scene interpretation. Exception for this dasakam: the post's pictures 2-10 (nostanza-01.jpg to nostanza-09.jpg) carry no caption and are mapped by post order to stanzas 2-10 ("mapping_basis": "post-order-uncaptioned"), each checked against its stanza; see order_based_mappings.

order_based_mappings.rule: Post order: picture N -> stanza N for pictures 2-10. Where a stanza's commentary clearly points to a different picture, map by commentary instead.
order_based_mappings.commentary_check: Stanzas 2-10 have no commentary on disk (the pictures are uncaptioned and no other source is supplied), and stanza 1's caption describes stanza 1 only, so no commentary points to a different picture. Each picture was checked against its stanza's verse instead; none was moved.
order_based_mappings.source: Captain's answer of 2026-11-27 ("For now use them in order you can match with commentry ..") on the Facebook group read-back (missing-stanza search), which found no caption for pictures 2-10 of this post

2.picture_shows: A fierce horned asura standing in fire with a mace.
2.verse_check: The verse names Vrikasura as the example of worshippers of quickly-pleased gods who come to ruin; the picture introduces Vrikasura.

3.picture_shows: Shiva holding arrows, a devotee bowing before him with folded hands.
3.verse_check: The verse has Shakuni's son asking Narada which god is quickly pleased and being sent to worship Shiva; the picture shows that worship of Shiva (Narada is not shown).

4.picture_shows: Shiva appearing beside a sacrificial fire, reaching toward a seated man who clutches his head.
4.verse_check: The verse has the asura's severe penance, his move to cut off his head on the seventh day, Shiva appearing and the boon of death by a hand on the head; the picture shows that moment.

5.picture_shows: A man with raised hand chasing a fleeing Shiva (trident, damaru), Parvati behind.
5.verse_check: The verse has the freed asura chasing Shiva, who flees looking back, until Vishnu stands before the asura as a young brahmachari; the picture shows the chase (the brahmachari is not shown).

6.picture_shows: Parvati, Shiva with trident, and a blue asura with fiery hair, raised hands, in a dance-like group.
6.verse_check: The verse has the brahmachari's words and the asura putting his hand on his own head and falling; the picture shows the asura with Shiva and Parvati but neither the brahmachari nor the fall. Weakest fit; no other picture shows this scene and no commentary points elsewhere, so post order is kept.

7.picture_shows: Two panels: a sage with a water pot below Brahma's court in the clouds; Shiva in anger on a mountain with trident, Parvati and Nandi, and a sage with folded hands.
7.verse_check: The verse has the sages on the Sarasvati sending Bhrigu to test the three gods, Brahma's anger and Shiva about to strike, restrained by Parvati; the picture shows both tests.

8.picture_shows: A sage kicking Vishnu reclining on Adisesha, Lakshmi seated beside.
8.verse_check: The verse has Bhrigu kicking Vishnu asleep on Lakshmi's lap and Vishnu rising gladly to ask his pardon; the picture shows the kick.

9.picture_shows: A crowned sage with folded hands before a standing four-armed Vishnu, assembled rishis worshipping.
9.verse_check: The verse has the Sarasvati sages, now certain, devoting themselves to Vishnu and attaining liberation; the picture shows the sages' worship of Vishnu.

10.picture_shows: Krishna playing the flute in a starry sky, standing on water.
10.verse_check: The verse is the closing prayer to the Lord of Guruvayur, the gopis' fortune; the picture shows Krishna.
